questions.question: Does the resolver's reusable set really EQUAL the exported policy's set for every configuration load_catalog_config admits (explicit true, explicit false, unset, kind-not-listed, kind-listed, unknown field, duplicate root ids)? Where can they still diverge, and is the divergence fail-open or fail-closed?
questions.answer: For policy.export_policy (v1) the answer is YES by construction, and I verified it end-to-end through the live loader for 10 shapes with a real temp catalog + resolve per shape (b01_review_config_matrix.json): 1 unset+kind-listed -> effective/v1/v2 all true, resolver reused_exact; 2 false+listed -> all false, missing; 3 unset+unlisted -> all false, missing; 4 true+unlisted -> all true, reused_exact (a WIDENING versus pre-0e28d99, which returned missing for this shape); 5 false+unlisted -> all false, missing; 6 reusable_for_filing: "false" (quoted) -> all TRUE, reused_exact; 7 "true" on read_only:false -> all TRUE, reused_exact (CFG-05 keys on `is True`, so the read_only/adapter checks are skipped); 8 [] -> all false, missing; 9 unknown root field -> CatalogConfigError 'roots[0] unknown fields'; 10 duplicate root_id -> CatalogConfigError 'duplicate root_id (CFG-03)'. So there is no admitted configuration in which the resolver's set differs from export_policy's set. For the artifact the consumer actually consumes (export_policy_2x / _policy_export_payload) agreement holds today only because policy_2x._effective_reusable_2x is a TEXTUALLY IDENTICAL COPY, not because the code is shared: that is the one live divergence path, and it is reachable by a one-line edit (mutation x2_kind_only: the consumer allowance becomes {company_raw,dropbox_stock} while the resolver's rule set stays {company_raw}). That divergence is FAIL-OPEN for the consumer: filing-fetch's containment allowance would include a root the wiki's own rule refuses (it would accept a handle under a root the wiki refuses to reuse). Two further type-level notes, both fail-open and both pre-existing (policy.py/config.py are untouched by 0e28d99): a quoted "false" is read as true by bool(), and a quoted "true" bypasses CFG-05. Everything else is fail-closed.

questions.question: Can the new candidate-level filter silently turn a request that was answerable BEFORE the change into MISSING for a root that was effectively reusable before (ids != kinds, empty sets, several roots with one kind, an explicitly-false root holding the only copy, and the `not reusable_root_ids or ...` branch when the set is empty)?
questions.answer: No silent miss was found in any shape I could construct. (1) ids != kinds: probed (root_id dropbox_stock / future_lake, kind directory) - filtered by root_id, works. (2) Several roots with the same kind: probed (first_raw false prio 10 / second_raw unset prio 20, both kind company_raw) - shipped 0e28d99 serves the reusable second_raw copy, the pre-B01 rule serves the excluded first_raw copy. (3) Explicitly-false root holding the only copy (fixture A): the answer becomes MISSING, which is the intended R-2 narrowing, and it is NOT silent - the trace carries '<title>: no_reusable_root_location' and the request was never 'effectively reusable' by the exported rule (the export said false before the change too); filing-fetch then takes its download path instead of reuse. (4) Empty set: unreachable as a filter case - when no root is effectively reusable the document-level gate at resolver.py:1102-1109 rejects first ('no_reusable_root_location') and _handle/_select_candidate are never called; instrumented counts are `select_calls=[]` for both the all-non-reusable fixture and fixture A (b01_review_causal.json). (5) The `not reusable_root_ids or ...` escape: because of (4) it is dead code on the resolve() path (resolve is the only caller of _handle, and _handle the only caller of _select_candidate - grep over src), and removing it (mutation `no_escape`) leaves all 6 acceptance cases green. Its direction is nevertheless fail-open: a future direct caller of _handle/_select_candidate that omits the argument gets NO filtering at all. The only narrowing the filter adds beyond the document gate is the intended one (candidates from explicitly-false roots); whenever the document gate passes, at least one candidate carries a reusable root_id, so the filter cannot empty a list the gate admitted.

questions.question: Is pinning the cross-repo policy_sha256 in a wiki contract test the right coupling, or a maintenance trap? What does filing-fetch actually consume, and does the pinned value match the shipped config?
questions.answer: The coupling is the right intent aimed at the wrong artifact. filing-fetch consumes (i) the resolve response's `policy_export`, which cli._policy_export_payload builds from export_policy_2x (hash + roots with path_ref), verifying _policy_document_hash(payload) == payload['policy_hash'] and requiring the handle's canonical path to live under a root the payload marks reusable_for_filing (filing_contracts.py:406-497), and (ii) the envelope's policy_hash, which it requires to equal the payload's hash when both are present (fetch_filing.py:889-930) - and the envelope's hash comes from the runtime policy snapshot, i.e. the wiki-internal invariant is runtime_policy.json.policy_hash == _policy_export_payload(config)['policy_hash']. filing-fetch holds NO literal expectation at all (searched: no 64-hex policy constant anywhere in the repo), so nothing on the consumer side has to be 'migrated' when the wiki's export changes - only the wiki's own runtime snapshot has to be re-derived. The value the acceptance case freezes (cf0ac2ad...) is export_policy v1, which no consumer reads; the value in play is c773099b... (measured), and it is exactly what the production .source_catalog/runtime_policy.json already carries. As shipped, the frozen literal therefore (a) does not protect the contract it advertises - a mutation of the 2x copy passes 6/6 - and (b) fires on any benign config edit (the v1 payload includes path/priority/routes), with a failure message telling the reader to migrate filing-fetch, which is not true. Recommended: freeze _policy_export_payload(load_catalog_config(SHIPPED))['policy_hash'] (or the payload's reusable-root set) and, if a cross-repo guard is wanted, assert the runtime-snapshot == payload invariant; a magic literal is acceptable only with an accurate message.

questions.question: Do the sampled B05 P2 fixes from 9826b3c hold - declaration bound to the value the scanner consumed, and agreeing captures accumulating as sources with their attribution - and does an own counter-example break the declaration rule?
questions.answer: Mostly yes, with one counter-example. `python -m pytest tests/contract/test_r4b05_metadata_provenance.py -q` -> 9 passed (the file's 9 cases = the commit message's '9 acceptance cases'). The accumulation/attribution half reproduces: after two agreeing captures the record keeps conflicts [] and carries >= 2 sources with non-null source_id, roles stored+incoming, none attributed to null/unknown. The declaration half holds for the value shapes the fix had in mind (a sidecar key the classifier ignores, e.g. document_kind '10-K', no longer counts as a declaration) but is under-inclusive for values the classifier transforms: _declared_columns compares raw vs used with exact trimmed string equality while _classification lowercases the sidecar kind, so document_kind 'Annual_Report' is consumed by the classifier yet recorded as derived. Counter-example (same bytes, same sidecar, only the literal's case changed; b01_review_declaration.json): control 'annual_report' -> stored quarterly_report corrected to annual_report, document_kind conflicts [], 1 annual_report candidate, resolve(annual_report)=reused_equivalent; variant 'Annual_Report' -> kind stays quarterly_report, document_kind sources declared=[false,false], 2 conflicts, metadata_status blocked, annual_report candidates 0, resolve(annual_report)=missing. Recommendation: normalise both sides (casefold/strip) or, better, have _classification report WHICH key/value it consumed so the declaration test can never drift from the classifier again - that is the root cause B-VR05-04 named.

questions.id: F-B01-7 (extra audit requested by the operator)
questions.question: Is the F-B01-7 justification sound, is strict=True the right mechanism, and does the change weaken the other four corruption variants?
questions.answer: The justification is SOUND and I reproduced it without relying on the author's monkeypatch probe: with the real 0e28d99^ tree the case's inline config (default reusable_root_kinds ('company_raw',), directory root) yields missing via the reuse gate, while under a production-shaped kind list the document resolves both before and after the change, and it resolves again after deleting the sidecar and re-scanning (5 combinations, plus the location_inactive variant which still fails closed via no_canonical_active_location). The entity gate is active in every run, so no identity check was removed; the read layer genuinely answers from the index (2 location rows, 3 document_entities rows survive the sidecar deletion). strict=True is the right mechanism and does what is claimed: an XPASS is reported as a FAILURE, so B06 implementing the rule forces deliberate removal of the marker; the requirement is registered in the B06 row of test-acceptance-map.md. The other four variants are untouched (marker + comments only) and still pass; the caveat is that an xfail accepts ANY failure, so the marked variant stops reporting unrelated breakage (my mechanism probe shows an unrelated RuntimeError also ending as xfailed) - narrowing it to raises=AssertionError would keep that signal.

Consequently (i) the claim 'the resolver calls the same function as the export, so resolver and export can no longer disagree' is false for the export that matters - policy_2x._effective_reusable_2x is still an independent copy - and (ii) the advertised guard does not exist: a change to that copy (or to the 2x payload) breaks/loosens the consumer containment with no wiki test failing.
findings.evidence: (1) cli.py:835-857 `_policy_export_payload` = verbatim export_policy_2x document + hash, called at cli.py:811 and :1182 to fill the resolve response's `policy_export`; (2) filing_contracts.py:449-497 verifies `_policy_document_hash(policy_snapshot)` against the payload's own hash and derives the containment allowance from that payload's reusable_for_filing/path_ref roots - and grep finds NO 64-hex policy literal anywhere in filing-fetch, so the consumer re-derives it; (3) measured on the shipped config: export_policy v1 = cf0ac2adf9714fe003eb1d1497d678877840e35a6a6c32bc65aa7e5d0c0e1626 (the frozen value, b01_review_hash.json pinned_equals_v1=true, pinned_equals_2x=false) vs _policy_export_payload/export_policy_2x = c773099b3dcfa2cc0f8e4b1c3e2f783f9c8f9715a415ba708c12bf79398675dd, which is also the policy_hash of the production .source_catalog/runtime_policy.json (the value the resolve envelope and filing-fetch's close-gap binding carry); (4) the run directory contradicts itself: file-scope.md §2 and field-owner-map.json:40 both name export_policy_2x as the ONLY source of filing-fetch's FC-501 policy_hash, while field-owner-map.json:95-96 reports and pins the v1 hash as that cross-repo value; (5) mutation x2_kind_only (one-line revert of the 2x copy) -> 6 passed, payload hash 24d3274739cab24fc22747dc3a08eea446697e3a591863ba31a9eb43e010b999 -> 00cb882c585ef338dc833a44148a504b08517db4c283a79ab5dbd10541cabd84, consumer allowance {company_raw,dropbox_stock} vs resolver set {company_raw} (fail-open drift; b01_review_2x_divergence.json).
findings.impact: The step's headline guarantee ('the resolver and the exported containment policy can never disagree') rests on two identical copies rather than one implementation, and the guard that is supposed to fail loudly when they drift is aimed at an artifact no consumer reads. A future edit to policy_2x.py (the file S-3 freezes precisely because it is the cross-repo source) would silently widen filing-fetch's containment allowance while the wiki test suite stays green. No wrong bytes are served today: the two copies agree, and the shipped config's answers are unchanged.
findings.required_action: Point the freeze at the consumed artifact - assert `_policy_export_payload(load_catalog_config(SHIPPED_CONFIG))['policy_hash']` == c773099b3dcfa2cc0f8e4b1c3e2f783f9c8f9715a415ba708c12bf79398675dd and the payload's reusable-root set - and correct the word 'cross-repo' wherever cf0ac2ad is presented as the FC-501 hash (commit message, findings F-B01-6, evidence/b01-implementation.md §3/§4, progress.md, checkpoint.json, field-owner-map.json shipped_config_facts). If the reviewer's aim is 'one implementation', have policy_2x._effective_reusable_2x call policy._effective_reusable (its output is byte-identical for every admitted configuration, so S-3's frozen-payload rule is respected) and keep a hash-freeze on the payload as the migration alarm.

findings.claim: Misattributed causal claim: F-B01-6 and evidence/b01-implementation.md §2.1 state that test_r4b01_explicit_false_is_not_reusable 'went RED first - observed exactly the excluded root's copy being served - and turned green only after the candidate-level filter was added'. That case never needed the filter and cannot detect its removal.
findings.evidence: Instrumented runs (b01_review_causal.json, fixture A_single_false): shipped and filter-neutralised runs are indistinguishable - status missing, trace ['entity_gate_rejected: 0','2025: no_reusable_root_location'], `_select_candidate` call count 0 - because the single excluded root makes the effective set empty and the document-level gate rejects first. Mutation filter_off against a copy of the shipped file: 1 failed, 5 passed, and the failure is test_r4b01_resolver_set_matches_the_exported_policy (three roots, excluded copy at rank 1); reverting the set rule (kind_only) is what makes test_r4b01_explicit_false_is_not_reusable fail. The underlying gap ('the group gate alone is not enough, the winner can be an excluded root's copy') is TRUE and IS pinned - by the fourth case - so only the attribution is wrong.
findings.impact: A future reviewer looking for the guard of the candidate-level filter would test the wrong case; anyone re-deriving the step's history from the record gets an inverted causal story. No product behaviour depends on this sentence.
findings.required_action: Rewrite the sentence in findings.md F-B01-6 and evidence/b01-implementation.md §2.1: the case that goes RED without the candidate-level filter is test_r4b01_resolver_set_matches_the_exported_policy (its rank-1 copy sits under the explicitly-false root); test_r4b01_explicit_false_is_not_reusable is decided by the set computation (the document-level gate) alone.

findings.claim: The sampled B-VR05-04 fix is under-inclusive: 'a key counts as a declaration only when the value the scanner actually used IS that key's value' is implemented as exact trimmed string equality, while _classification consumes the sidecar document_kind case-insensitively. A genuinely declared, case-variant kind is therefore recorded as DERIVED, its precedence over a derived stored value is lost, and a false conflict plus a silent MISSING are produced.
findings.evidence: _declared_columns (scanner.py:1263-1289) compares str(raw).strip() == str(used).strip(); _classification (scanner.py:125) lowercases: str(metadata.get('document_kind') or '').strip().lower(). Own counter-example, same fixture twice with only the literal's case changed (b01_review_declaration.json): control document_kind 'annual_report' -> stored quarterly_report corrected to annual_report, document_kind conflicts [], 1 annual_report candidate, resolve(annual_report)=reused_equivalent; variant 'Annual_Report' -> stored kind stays quarterly_report, document_kind sources declared=[false,false] (no true), 2 conflicts, metadata_status blocked, annual_report candidates 0, resolve(annual_report)=missing. The committed file's 9 cases pass (9 passed) - the shape is simply not covered.
findings.impact: A declaration the classifier honoured can be silently downgraded, which both weakens the 'declared beats derived' rule the fix was protecting and manufactures a blocked/false conflict; in the losing direction the document becomes unresolvable for the declared kind with an empty resolve trace (the pre-existing silent-miss pattern of B-VR05-03), so a consumer sees 'no such document'.
findings.required_action: Normalise both sides before comparing (casefold + strip, mirroring _classification), or better, make _classification return which key/value produced the column and bind declaredness to that value - the drift between the declaration test and the classifier is the root cause B-VR05-04 identified. Add a case with a case-variant (and a whitespace-padded) declared kind.

findings.claim: The step's 'an explicit declaration takes effect' guarantee is configuration-dependent: load_catalog_config admits non-boolean reusable_for_filing literals, and bool() then inverts the declared intent. A quoted "false" is reused (fail-open), and a quoted "true" bypasses CFG-05/CFG-07 (the read_only and adapter-capability checks key on `is True`).
findings.evidence: Config-shape matrix through the live loader (b01_review_config_matrix.json): shape 6 `reusable_for_filing: "false"` (kind company_raw, kinds [company_raw]) -> _effective_reusable True, v1 True, v2 True, resolver reused_exact (the declarer's intent was NOT reusable); shape 7 `reusable_for_filing: "true"` with read_only: false -> admitted (no CFG-05 error), all flags True, resolver reused_exact. policy.py:70-72 `if spec.reusable_for_filing is not None: return bool(spec.reusable_for_filing)` and config.py:108-118 (`is True` guards) are untouched by 0e28d99, so this is pre-existing and both the resolver and both exports agree - there is no divergence, only an inverted declaration.
findings.impact: A future operator who quotes the flag (a very common YAML slip) gets the opposite of what they declared, silently and fail-open; the same slip also skips the read_only/adapter admission checks designed to constrain reusable external roots. The shipped config is unaffected (bare true / unset).
findings.required_action: Type-check the field at the single admission point (bool or null, else CatalogConfigError) - it is one line in config.py's per-root validation - or at minimum record the literal-type caveat next to the semantics table in b-design §B01.2 and the field-owner-map.

findings.claim: The candidate filter's `not reusable_root_ids or ...` escape is dead code on the resolve() path, and its documented rationale ('the empty set means no filtering, preserving the old callers' behaviour') describes a caller that does not exist - while its direction is fail-open for any future direct caller.
findings.evidence: resolve() is the only caller of _handle and _handle the only caller of _select_candidate (grep over src/company_wiki/source_catalog). When the effective set is empty, the document-level gate at resolver.py:1102-1109 rejects before _handle: instrumented `_select_candidate` call count 0 for fixture A_single_false and for the all-non-reusable fixture (b01_review_causal.json). Mutation no_escape (removing the clause) survives all 6 acceptance cases. The author's own note in evidence/b01-implementation.md §2 ('集合为空 = 不过滤，保持旧调用方的行为') is therefore inaccurate in its reason, though the branch is currently harmless.
findings.impact: A latent trap: if B06/B07 or a future refactor calls _handle/_select_candidate directly without threading the set, the default frozenset() silently disables reuse filtering (fail-open) while resolve() would have failed closed. The same default also makes the filter's contract invisible at the call site.
findings.required_action: Either drop the escape (the document gate already guarantees a non-empty set whenever _select_candidate runs) or make the parameter mandatory (no default) so an omitted argument is a TypeError instead of a silent fail-open; correct the rationale text.

findings.claim: Record precision: (a) evidence/b01-implementation.md §3.2 labels '4 passed' as the FC-1204 complexity ratchet, but that file has exactly 2 tests (2 passed); the 4 belongs to the complexity + coverage tables together (the coverage table only passes after a fresh coverage run - the tracked coverage.json is stale, carry-over B-VR05-08). (b) The b6d1fdc xfail accepts ANY failure, so the marked variant stops reporting unrelated breakage.
findings.evidence: (a) `python -m pytest tests/contract/test_fc1204_complexity_ratchet.py -q` -> 2 passed; with FC1204_COVERAGE_GATE=1 the coverage table reads the tracked coverage.json (last commit 90fb08d, 2026-09-01: service 94.42, scanner 90.49, resolver 85.64) and fails, while my fresh measurement gives resolver 87.95 / scanner 91.12 / service 95.20 with empty problem lists (b01_review_coverage.json). (b) b01_review_xfail_mechanism.py: a parametrization whose body raises RuntimeError is still reported as xfailed under xfail(strict=True), while a passing body is reported as FAILED '[XPASS(strict)]'.
findings.impact: A reader cannot reproduce 'the ratchet is green' from the committed tree alone (they must regenerate coverage.json first - already noted as B-VR05-08), and the sidecar_missing variant can no longer distinguish 'still unimplemented' from 'broken in a new way'.
findings.required_action: (a) Say 'FC-1204 ratchet tables: complexity 2 passed, coverage green against a fresh --cov-branch coverage.json (the committed coverage.json is stale)'. (b) Optionally add raises=AssertionError to the xfail (or a follow-up assertion that the failure is the documented one) so unexpected exceptions are not swallowed; the B06 acceptance item already exists in test-acceptance-map.md:15.
